subject: Next steps: NovaCorp reranker integration & evaluation plan

Subject: Follow-up + architecture questions from today's call

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks for the call earlier — good discussion. We wanted to capture the follow-ups from our side so we can align on an evaluation plan before the pilot. High-level ask: we want to validate a reranker inserted after our retrieval stage (ElasticSearch -> candidate set) and compare quality/cost trade-offs across a few model variants.

Specific questions we need answered so we can prep a test set and run an initial eval:
- What exact API endpoints would we call for a per-query rerank vs a batch rerank? (we do ~200 qps at peak but only rerank top-200 candidates)
- What auth options does Redwood support for private deployments? We prefer mTLS but may start with API keys.
- How do you recommend tuning top_k (we're thinking eval at k=200 but production may be k<=10)?
- What evaluation metrics do you recommend for relevance (MRR, NDCG@5/10, Recall@k, others)?
- Any guidance on creating negatives / synthetic distractors and labeling effort (approx label volume needed for stable signal)?
- Latency and cost ballpark for reranking 200 candidates with one of your medium quantized models (per-request p50/p95 and cost-per-1k-queries)?

We can provide a small sample file (100 queries + gold lists) if you want to run a dry eval on your side — would that be possible?

Next steps we propose:
1) Redwood to send an evaluation playbook + recommended default configs
2) We share a sample test set (100 queries) and baseline metrics by Friday 8/20
3) Follow-up call to review preliminary results the week of 8/24

Thanks,
Ethan

Subject: Re: Follow-up + architecture questions from today's call

Ethan — thanks for the succinct list, that helps. Quick replies inline, and Marissa will follow with a detailed playbook. Connor, looped for infra/auth notes.

- Endpoints: Redwood exposes a per-request rerank endpoint (/v1/rerank) and a batch endpoint (/v1/rerank/batch) for bulk scoring. Both accept a candidate list plus query context; batch supports up to 2k items per request when using streaming/batched mode.
- Auth: API keys are the default for hosted; Private supports API keys, mTLS, and KMS-backed key rotation.
- top_k: totally reasonable to eval at k=200; production guidance usually trims to k=5-20 depending on latency SLO. Marissa will include heuristics.
- Metrics & labeling: Marissa will enumerate.
- Latency/cost: ballparks below once we confirm model family and quantization. We'll include a sample config so you can simulate cost.

We'll attach a short playbook and a sample testset schema. Can you confirm: query distribution (avg length), average candidate size per query, and whether recency signals are required? Also which week is best for the results review (we suggested 8/24).

I'll send the playbook in the next email.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Lee <ethan.lee@novacorp.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-17T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood reranker evaluation playbook + recommendations (attached)

Ethan — attaching a short playbook (reranker-playbook.pdf) and a CSV sample we typically use. Key points below — I'll keep this practical so your DS team can start quickly.

1) Endpoints and payloads - Per-query rerank: POST /v1/rerank  payload: {"query": "...", "candidates": [{"id":"c1","text":"..."}, ...], "context": {...}} - Batch rerank: POST /v1/rerank/batch  payload: {"requests": [{"query":..., "candidates":[...]}, ...]}

2) Auth & network - Hosted: API key (bearer) + optional IP allowlist.
- Private: support for mTLS & API keys; KMS for rotating keys. Recommend mTLS for production pilot if you can provision certs.

3) Tuning top_k - Evaluation: keep top_k equal to your retrieval cutoff (k_eval = 200) to measure end-to-end quality.
- Production: start with top_k = 10 for web UX, 5 for ultra-low-latency endpoints. For dev/test, we use top_k=50 to inspect boundary cases.

4) Metrics (recommended battery) - MRR (Mean Reciprocal Rank)
- NDCG@5 and NDCG@10
- Recall@k (k=5,10,50)
- Precision@k if you have binary labels
- Pairwise AUC / Win rate for model-vs-baseline comparisons
- Significance testing: paired bootstrap / McNemar for thresholded decisions

5) Data & labeling guidance - Labeling: aim for 5-10k judged query-document pairs for stable NDCG signals across common queries; for a rapid pilot, 500-1k queries with graded labels can surface large regressions.
- Negatives: use in-batch negatives + hard negatives from retrieval baseline (elastic false positives). We typically synthesize distractors by sampling near-neighbors but ensure they are plausible.

6) Evaluation protocol - Holdout: 70/15/15 (train/val/test) if you plan to fine-tune.
- Use stratified sampling by query intent/volume.
- Compute per-query metrics and then summarize by macro-average and by traffic-weighted averages.

7) Cost & latency notes (ballpark) - If you rerank 200 candidates with a medium quantized reranker model in Redwood Dedicated: p50 ~ 35-45ms, p95 ~ 110-160ms (per-request; batch mode amortizes cost), cost ~ $X per 1k queries (we'll produce exact numbers once you pick model).

8) Practical recommendations - Start with a small corpus (100-500 queries) for sanity checks.
- Run A/B tests with MRR and CTR downstream if available.
- Log top_k distribution and token-level costs per request.

Attachments: reranker-playbook.pdf (9 pages) — includes sample eval script and recommended hyperparameters. I also attached a sample CSV with columns: query_id, query_text, candidate_id, candidate_text, label.

If you want, we can run an initial dry evaluation on the 100-query sample you mentioned and return NDCG/MRR numbers by end of week.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Retrieval
Redwood Inference

Ethan — quick infra notes that might affect your integration plan:

- Auth: if you choose mTLS, we'll need the cert chain and a list of client CNs; for API keys we recommend a service account with a scoped key and rotation every 30 days.
- Routing: we can route rerank traffic to a dedicated pool to isolate latency impact from other workloads; useful if you want strict p95 SLOs.
- Batching: for your traffic profile, consider batching groups of 8-16 queries for cheaper throughput during off-peak hours. For per-query online endpoints, enable continuous batching with a <5ms hold if your p50 budget allows.
- Observability: we'll provision a dashboard with token counts, p50/p95 per-route, and per-request cost.

I've attached a tiny sample testset (novacorp-testset-sample.csv) to show the format we expect.

Connor
Platform Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
